result.title: Spade-SLAM: Sparse Correspondence Anchors for Dense Self-Supervised Visual SLAM
result.summary: We introduce Spade-SLAM, a self-supervised dense visual SLAM framework that substantially narrows the long-standing performance gap to supervised methods in a zero-shot setting. By demonstrating that high-fidelity tracking can be achieved without explicit ground-truth pose and depth labels, our approach offers a highly effective and label-efficient alternative to fully supervised pretraining. Our core contribution is a complementary sparse-to-dense training regime: While a warping-based photometric loss provides a dense training signal, we stabilize the optimization and suppress drift in ambiguous regions using a sparse correspondence loss derived from image feature matches. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Spade-SLAM significantly improves robustness and accuracy compared to existing self-supervised baselines, closely rivaling SLAM systems trained with explicit pose and depth supervision. The code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/JulianPSchmitt/Spade-SLAM.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Spade-SLAM：一个自监督稠密视觉 SLAM 框架，在稠密光度损失之外引入由图像特征匹配得到的稀疏对应损失，以在无位姿与深度标签时稳定优化、抑制歧义区域漂移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「稀疏对应锚点约束稠密训练信号」的思路可能与 LVR 中用稀疏视觉证据锚定稠密 latent 状态、抑制歧义区域漂移的训练设计相通，可供核查；但论文本身不涉及多模态推理。
